Galop, an LGBTQ+ anti-abuse charity, called on the government to create an emergency national fund for specialist trans refuges, as many people were being turned away from mainstream services. items.title: ‘Scapegoating’: green groups condemn plan to axe Environment Agency and Natural England
items.desc: Ministers proposing to abolish the quangos in attempt to give politicians more control over what gets built and where Scientists have accused the government of scapegoating nature for proposing to scrap the only environmental regulator with a legal duty to protect the natural world. Louise Haigh, the de facto deputy prime minister, said on Monday that the independent regulator Natural England and the Environment Agency were being reviewed as part of a wider shake-up of quangos, or arm’s length bodies. Ministers are considering abolishing the two biggest environmental regulators in an attempt to give politicians greater control over what gets built and where. Continue reading...

But the various options for how Britain could rejoin the EU, or ‘Breturn’, will not be outlined until December. Pippa Crerar has been speaking to the prime minister about how he hopes to convince the public that reversing Brexit is worth the headache You can tell us what you think of Guardian podcasts with our survey here Send any questions for Pippa and Kiran to politicsweeklyuk@theguardian.com You can watch this episode of Politics Weekly on our YouTube channel here . items.title: Talk of scrapping Natural England smacks of a government not joining the dots
items.desc: Environmentalists say abolishing independent body will make it easier for landowners and developers ‘to trash nature’ Not just any quango, Natural England is the only public body that exists to legally protect the jewels in the crown of English nature – places increasingly under threat in a country that is overseeing an ongoing and devastating decline in its natural world. Ecologists who work for Natural England are independent, and have the legal duty to scrutinise political decisions and ensure that short-term gallops for growth are not allowed to bulldoze forever rare and declining habitats.
